findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/checklist.ts:981-985 [critical] The preflight launch revalidation callback only compares headHash, materialHash, and storyFilesHash. It does not revalidate the CLI/worktree, Git index, writer identity or lease, provider capability, resource budget, or writable evidence target after preflight and immediately before child launch, so those states can change in the gap and the command can start despite an invalid preflight contract, violating CHK-004:adversarial:0 and allowing nonzero command execution or partial evidence writes.

findings.desc: High: CertificationWindow accepts a stale causal advisory because CausalDependencyDecision has no current HEAD/materialHash/storyFilesHash binding. In packages/main/src/core/causal-evidence.ts:706-718 and 739-748, the decision carries only decision flags plus a self-hash; packages/main/src/core/certification-window.ts:703-715 verifies only that self-hash and gateAdmissible, then waives material drift whenever causalDecision=advisory and storyFilesHashAdvisory=true. Repro command: node --input-type=module -e with an advisory decision computed at currentMaterialHash=m2, then detectCertificationWindowMaterialDrift with live materialHash=m3 and the same storyFilesHash; observed {"decisionCurrentMaterial":"m2","liveMaterial":"m3","causalDecision":"advisory","decisionHashValid":true,"drift":{"drifted":false}}. A stale signed advisory can therefore keep specialized evidence admissible after a further material change; bind the decision to current material/HEAD/storyFilesHash and verify those bindings at consumption.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in bd9ba8e3e9 and verified by causal-evidence.test.mjs plus certification-window-smoke.js: the dependency decision now carries an identity-bound authority signature and certification-window evaluation rejects stale or forged causal advisory identity.

Causal dependency authority is process-local and cannot survive restart. packages/main/src/core/causal-evidence.ts:763-769 generates CAUSAL_DEPENDENCY_DECISION_KEY with randomBytes(32) at module load, while verifyCausalDependencyDecision at lines 924-948 recomputes the HMAC with that process-local key. Repro: create an advisory decision in one Node process, then import the same dist in a child and call verifyCausalDependencyDecision(decision, identity); the parent returns true and the child returns false. A signed/current CertificationWindow decision therefore becomes inadmissible after CLI or process restart, despite the acceptance contract requiring durable authority binding. Persist a stable authority key/signature or a verifiable durable authority artifact, and add a cross-process verification test.

Unknown input keys are silently excluded from dependency drift. packages/main/src/core/causal-evidence.ts:819-858 iterates each node.inputIds, but never checks keys present in currentInputHashes that are absent from the declared dependency DAG. Repro: evaluate a node declaring only declared=same while currentInputHashes also contains unmapped=changed, with materialHash changed and storyFilesHash unchanged; the function returns causalDecision=advisory, gateAdmissible=true, changedInputIds=[], and materialHashStrict=false. A changed dependency outside the declared nodes can therefore evade strict rerun or freshness handling. Enforce declared and current input-key completeness, or treat unknown keys as missing and take the strict materialHash fallback, with an adversarial test.

Receipt integrity is an unkeyed self-hash rather than authenticity. packages/main/src/core/causal-evidence.ts:359-365 and 368-384 accept any caller-recomputed SHA256 receiptHash; packages/main/src/core/store.ts:405-420 performs CAS checks under the supplied hash but adds no durable signature or authority binding. Repro: mutate persisted outputProbe from the original selector to EVIL, recompute receiptHash, update the index, and replay; the cache accepts EVIL with one child run, output {runs:1,first:pass,second:pass}. A local actor able to alter the artifact and index can manufacture a replayable PASS, violating tamper-resistant acceptance. Bind receipts to stable keyed authority or another non-caller-writable evidence source and add a tamper mutation test.

packages/main/src/core/causal-evidence.ts:272-280 [high] redactEnvironment uppercases every environment key before hashing the execution identity. On POSIX, effectiveValidationCommandEnvironment preserves case and the child process treats Path and PATH as distinct, but createCausalExecutionKey produces the same ce:v1 key and canonical PATH entry for both (repro on current HEAD: Path=a and PATH=a yield equal keys). A command whose behavior depends on a case-sensitive custom variable can therefore reuse a receipt under a different effective environment, violating the explicit environment identity and stale-cache acceptance=0 contract. Preserve POSIX key case and add a case-sensitive environment mutation test.

packages/main/src/core/causal-evidence.ts:608-619 [medium] The batch execution cache deletes an entry only when its promise resolves to a non-reusable receipt; if executeFresh rejects (for example a transient child/receipt-store I/O error), the derived batchReceipt remains a rejected promise in batch.executions. A later exact-key retry therefore returns the same rejection without invoking the child again (current-HEAD repro: first transient, second transient, runs=1). This permanently poisons the batch and violates the transaction/infra-failure retry contract; delete the same promise in a rejection handler and add a transient-error retry test.

packages/main/src/handlers/verifier.ts:499-510,624-635 [high] createValidationCausalPreflightGate rechecks canonicalized preflight facts before each child, but probeVerifierIndex records only readable/path and never fingerprints the Git index bytes or identity. Replacing or changing .git/index between the initial PASS and child launch therefore leaves factsUnchanged true, so validate can launch an expensive child against a stale current-index contract, violating CHK-004:adversarial:0/1. Include an index content digest or equivalent index identity in the verifier facts and revalidation.

packages/main/src/handlers/checklist.ts:1419-1431 [high] commitCanonicalCausalEvidence revalidate checks only head/material/storyFiles hashes and CAS index; it never re-reads the writer lease or validates the receipt command/effective-environment/selector-policy identity at canonical commit/retry. If the lease is revoked or expired or the execution identity changes after the preflight or child run, the checklist import still commits. This violates CHK-002 lease/index/material/identity revalidation; make the import transaction revalidate the complete writer and identity snapshot.

packages/main/src/handlers/checklist.ts:1254-1363,2417-2476 [high] the re-executing stale-refresh path runs enforceAndStampEvidence outside the checklist lock, then writeStaleRefresh writes the pre-refresh head/material/storyFiles hashes and receipt directly with store.writeChecklist. It never recomputes current identity or passes the new receipt through commitCanonicalCausalEvidence/importCausalEvidenceReceipt. A material, lease, or index change while the command runs can therefore persist mechanical true evidence bound to a stale snapshot as if it were fresh. Revalidate and import the receipt atomically before the refresh write.

packages/main/src/core/causal-evidence.ts:608-620 [medium] the batch cache removes a non-reusable receipt only in the fulfillment branch. If executeFresh rejects, for example on a runner or spawn infrastructure error, batchReceipt rejects and remains in args.batch.executions, so every later same-key intent reuses the rejection and cannot retry or reach a later PASS. This is distinct from the resolved fail, timeout, or partial-output case covered by F-007; remove the entry on rejection or finally as well.

packages/main/src/core/causal-evidence.ts:640-642,905-931 [high] executeCausalEvidence verifies only the preflight report's self-signature and all-pass shape; CausalPreflightFacts carries no command, storyId, or execution-identity binding, and the core never compares the report to the key being executed. Repro: preflightCausalEvidence(all-pass facts) with no command field, followed by executeCausalEvidence with a different command identity and revalidateBeforeRun=()=>true, returned disposition=executed with runs=1. A preflight for another command/story, or a caller-synthesized all-pass report, can therefore pass the launch gate. Bind the signed preflight to the same execution identity/current probes or make the authoritative handler boundary unavoidable.
